result.summary: Landlord Quinn clearly approved the lock replacement and new keys (event 006), so I recorded the approval and moved the job to provider selection. I couldn't assign a locksmith because none is named or on record for this property, so I've passed that to the agency. I also emailed the tenant to ask whether the door is secure, since that decides how urgent the job is. A hold has been set with a follow-up in 1 day.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 006 is a clear approval: classify_reply gave approve 0.98 with autonomy 'auto'. The landlord's request for keys for the tenant, landlord and agency matches the original scope, so it isn't a condition. I couldn't pick a contractor without making one up, because the ticket has no contractor, the property has no job history and the landlord named nobody. The intake classifier flagged a safety risk (0.81) because we don't know whether the door is secure, so I asked the tenant directly.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No contractor is named or on record, and inventing one would break the rule against making up facts.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat as an emergency and dispatch now
alternatives_considered.why_not: Nothing in the records says the door is insecure; the report only says the key snapped. I've asked the tenant and told them to call straight away if the door can't be secured.
The approval was clear, so the job should keep moving.
